title: Ethereum Fraud Detection
summary: Binary classification of Ethereum addresses as fraudulent or legitimate on 9,841 addresses with 50 transaction-derived features. LightGBM reaches F1 0.987 on held-out data, but the interesting part is what it took to trust that number: a group-aware split that removes the 5.7% of test rows a naive split would have leaked.

title: CrossW
summary: A crossword site where the theme lives in the clue rather than the word. ТРАМВАЙ is an ordinary word; "the transport that beheaded Berlioz" makes it belong to The Master and Margarita. Four themed packs, thirty-two puzzles, with no word repeated across levels. Answers never reach the browser in readable form.

title: Voronoi Path Planner
summary: An interactive robot path planner that does not just find a route but finds the safest one. It builds a clearance field against the obstacles, binary-searches the largest clearance threshold for which start and goal are still connected, then runs Dijkstra inside that corridor.

title: Computational Geometry in OpenGL
summary: Seven OpenGL programs across five labs, working up from a shaded triangle to real geometry: Bresenham against Xiaolin Wu line rasterization side by side, segment intersection by orientation test, Graham scan convex hull, and ear-clipping polygon triangulation.

title: Numerical Methods
summary: Eight self-contained labs in Octave, each with its own write-up and generated figures: interpolation on uniform against Chebyshev nodes (where the plots turn out to show monomial-basis conditioning rather than the Runge phenomenon), splines, least squares, Simpson integration with Runge error control, Runge-Kutta with adaptive stepping, and an Adams predictor-corrector checked against ode45.

title: Blockchain Papers
summary: Two papers written for a blockchain technology course: one on where blockchain and machine learning actually meet rather than where the marketing says they do, and one on bin packing as an NP-complete problem, with the approximation algorithms that make it tractable in practice.

title: Networked Tic-Tac-Toe
summary: A Qt client for a multiplayer game server: player list, invitation handshake with accept and decline, turn synchronisation and game-over detection. The Boost.Asio transport underneath is a third-party course library, stated as such.

title: Battleship
summary: Battleship on Qt with the domain kept strictly out of the UI: Board, Ship and Game know nothing about widgets, and BoardWidget does the painting. Builds against Qt6; the Qt5 fallback in the CMake file has not been compiled.
